items.t: Which ETFs have secured top-tier returns after a sluggish first half?
sum: Secondary battery-themed exchange-traded funds (ETFs), which had been overlooked due to the concentration of semiconductor large-cap stocks in the first half, have recently claimed top positions in three-month returns. Despite sluggishness in the electric vehicle market, a traditional key revenue source, expectations for energy storage system (ESS) demand and the commercialization of all-solid-state batteries have boosted investor sentiment.

According to KOSCOM ETF Check on the 22nd, the return (based on reinvestment of distributions) for "SOL All-Solid-State Battery & Silicon Anode Material" over the past three months as of that day was 23.55%. This is the highest return among all ETFs listed in Korea. Funds such as "KODEX All-Solid-State Battery ESS TOP2 Plus" (23.33%) and "KoAct Hydrogen Power ESS Infrastructure Active" (18.65%) also recorded positive returns, securing positions within the top 10.
Investment funds are also flowing in. In particular, KODEX All-Solid-State Battery ESS TOP2 Plus surpassed 200 billion won in net asset value approximately four months after its listing on June 23.

Experts in the financial investment industry cite the expansion of ESS demand and the commercialization of all-solid-state batteries as the reasons behind the high returns of secondary battery-themed ETFs. ESS is a device that stores generated electricity and supplies it when needed, gaining attention as renewable energy demand driven by AI data centers increases. This is because renewable energy sources such as solar and wind power see their electricity generation fluctuate depending on weather conditions. Additionally, all-solid-state batteries are a technology that replaces conventional liquid electrolytes with solids to enhance safety and energy density.

Kim Jung-hyun, head of the ETF Business Group at Shinhan Asset Management, said, "If investment targets in secondary batteries expanded from battery manufacturers in 2021-2022 to material companies such as cathode materials in 2023-2024, going forward, performance recovery through ESS and the competitiveness of next-generation technologies like all-solid-state batteries will become key factors determining corporate valuation."

sum: - Elevra Lithium has signed a binding spodumene concentrate supply agreement with a major battery maker
- The supply comes from the North American Lithium mine in Quebec and keeps exposure to market prices
- A separate sale of the Ghana project is still waiting on government approval ahead of a key deadline

Elevra Lithium (ASX:ELV) Basic Materials Elevra Lithium Limited (ASX:ELV) 3.16 AUD +0.010 0.318% Last Updated at: 2026-11-03T05:10:00Z has signed a binding spodumene concentrate supply agreement with battery maker LG Energy Solution, locking in a customer for output from its North American Lithium mine in Quebec. The agreement, announced in early October, comes as the company also works through the sale of its Ghana project and prepares to report its September quarter results next week. LG Energy Solution is a constituent of the ASX 200. For readers following ASX Lithium Stocks, the development adds a fresh reference point.

The contract is a multi-year, binding supply agreement for spodumene concentrate, starting from the earliest shipment, which is expected this year. Contracted volumes step up gradually, with a modest initial year followed by larger deliveries as the operation ramps, and there is scope for additional optional volume if both sides agree.

All of the material comes from North American Lithium, known as NAL, the Quebec mine and concentrator that Elevra owns outright. The deal gives the plant a committed home for a meaningful share of what it produces.

Pricing under the agreement is linked to the market and adjusted for lithium content, rather than fixed. That means Elevra stays exposed to price moves in both directions, rather than locking in a level that may later look too low or too high.

Expectations that the ESS market will expand faster on the back of growing artificial intelligence data center investment also supported the gains.

Samsung SDI (006400) traded at 588,000 won as of 2:15 p.m. on the 19th, up 10.94% from the previous session, according to the Korea Exchange. LG Energy Solution (373220) rose 6.33% to 428,500 won, while SK Innovation (096770) gained 6.25% to 161,500 won. On the KOSDAQ market, EcoPro (086520) advanced 7.87% to 87,700 won and EcoPro BM (247540) rose 6.27% to 113,600 won. The gains spread across the entire value chain, from finished battery manufacturing to materials supply.

Driving the buying was the prospect of a shift in the competitive landscape of the U.S. ESS market. Taiwanese technology publication DigiTimes reported that Chinese ESS companies have effectively withdrawn en masse from their U.S. operations this year because of tough American regulations, tariff burdens and strict equity screening. The report fueled expectations that Korean battery and ESS companies will gain market share in the United States, lifting their shares.

Rising ESS demand tied to expanding AI data center investment is also drawing attention. Among major clean power sources, solar and wind output varies with weather and time of day. ESS, which stores electricity and supplies it when needed, can offset that variability. A series of brokerage analyses showing the North American ESS market growing faster than expected has drawn investor interest. Brokerages are focusing on record-high new ESS installations in North America in the second quarter and on U.S. companies' intensifying efforts to reduce reliance on China.

"If Chinese companies pull out of the U.S. market, Korean companies are likely to benefit," an official in the securities industry said. "But we need to look closely at the actual scale of the withdrawal and how much it will lift earnings at individual Korean companies."

Battery stocks, by contrast, are drawing inflows. Sentiment toward the battery sector, which had languished amid the electric-vehicle chasm, has improved as it secures rapidly growing energy storage systems (ESS) driven by AI data-center expansion as a new growth engine.

LG Energy Solution, Samsung SDI See ESS Revenue Share Near 30% as EV Demand Slows
sum: AI Data Center Power Demand Drives ESS Growth as Battery Makers Shift Production From EVs

The share of energy storage systems, or ESS, in the total revenue of LG Energy Solution and Samsung SDI is expected to rise from the 20% range in the second quarter to the mid-30% range by the end of the year. Demand for ESS is growing as power consumption from artificial intelligence data centers surges in North America, while battery makers are accelerating the conversion of production lines to ESS products to offset slowing electric vehicle demand.

According to battery industry sources and securities analysts on Aug. 17, ESS accounted for 28% of LG Energy Solution’s revenue in the second quarter, up steadily from 22.7% in the fourth quarter of last year. ESS revenue is projected to rise to 2.98 trillion won, or approximately $2.11 billion, in the third quarter and 3.85 trillion won in the fourth quarter, pushing its share of total revenue to an estimated 37.3% in the fourth quarter. At Samsung SDI, the ESS revenue share is expected to increase from 20.6% in the second quarter to 35.1% in the fourth quarter.

The main drivers of the shift in revenue mix are the expansion of AI data centers and increased investment in power grids in North America. ESS demand, which was previously driven largely by conventional power-generation projects, is increasingly shifting toward large-scale and long-duration systems as AI data centers expand. LG Energy Solution secured more than 3 trillion won in new ESS orders during the first half of this year, including projects involving AI data centers.

One example is the Steel River Energy Project in Arkansas, being developed by Google and U.S. power-generation company CCE. LG Energy Solution is supplying batteries for the 2.9-gigawatt ESS project, which will be combined with 2.5 gigawatts of solar power generation. Industry analysts expect higher plant utilization to translate directly into improved earnings as the cost burden from production-line conversions in the first half subsides.

items.t: LG Energy Solution Targets 2029 for Dry Electrode Mass Production, Aiming to Undercut China with 30% Cost Cut
sum: LG Energy Solution (373220) will begin full-scale mass production of dry electrode process technology—dubbed a game changer in the battery industry—starting in 2029. The strategy is to upend the China-dominated LFP (lithium iron phosphate) battery market by slashing production costs by up to 30% through this innovative method of manufacturing electrodes without liquid solvents.

"LFP is the field where applying dry electrodes delivers the most definitive impact in terms of performance and price," said Yoon Sung-soo, Senior Vice President of Advanced Process Technology at LG Energy Solution, in an interview with the Seoul Economic Daily on the 27th. "We have completed a pilot line in Ochang and are continuing development work, with the goal of mass-producing LFP batteries using the dry process from 2029." Should LG Energy Solution succeed in producing LFP electrodes in 2029, it would be a world first. Even Tesla, which is regarded as being ahead in dry process development, has yet to apply the technology to LFP batteries.

The dry electrode process is a method of forming electrode sheets by compacting active materials in solid powder form, as opposed to the conventional wet process where active materials, conductive additives, and binders are mixed into a liquid solvent, coated onto electrodes, and then dried. At LG Energy Solution's Daejeon Technology Research Center, researchers are refining the technology by examining fundamental properties—such as thickness, loading levels, and adhesion strength of samples produced on dry electrode equipment—as well as verifying the uniform coating state of cathode materials under ultra-precision microscopes.

The greatest advantage of the dry process is price competitiveness. It dramatically shortens production line length by eliminating the need for large-scale equipment used to dry and recover liquid solvents. This reduces the factory footprint, cutting total investment costs by roughly 30%, while lowering power consumption for drying equipment trims production costs by approximately 17%. "Initially, investment costs will be reduced by about 10% compared to the wet process," Senior Vice President Yoon explained.

sum: South Korea will open the door to single-stock leveraged ETFs as early as May 22, in a regulatory shift aimed at expanding higher-risk investment products.
The Cabinet approved the rule revision Tuesday. It takes effect April 28, with the first products likely to launch in late May, subject to filings and exchange approval.

The Financial Services Commission said only large-cap, highly liquid domestic stocks will be eligible, citing investor protection and market stability. To qualify, a stock must account for at least 10 percent of benchmark market capitalization and 5 percent of trading volume over the past three months — a threshold currently met only by Samsung Electronics and SK hynix.
Both 2x leveraged and inverse ETFs will be permitted, allowing investors to amplify exposure to price gains or declines in individual stocks.
Separately, the FSC will broaden ETF-linked derivatives. Weekly options, currently limited to stock indices, will be extended to individual stocks and ETFs.

Weekly options on individual stocks — initially limited to Samsung Electronics, SK hynix, Hyundai Motor and LG Energy Solution — are set to launch on June 29, with ETF-based weekly options to follow later this year. The FSC also plans to introduce more frequent expiry cycles for index options and monthly options linked to ETFs.
The changes are expected to expand trading strategies, including income-focused products such as covered call ETFs tied to domestic assets.

items.t: LG Energy Solution Declares Major Business Restructuring, Aims to Expand ESS Share to Mid-40% Range
sum: LG Energy Solution (373220) is embarking on a full-scale effort to move beyond its electric vehicle (EV)-centric business structure and build a balanced portfolio centered on Energy Storage Systems (ESS) and new ventures. The company plans to significantly increase the proportion of ESS and new businesses from the current level of approximately 20% to the mid-40% range in the future.

LG Energy Solution held its 6th regular shareholders' meeting at the LG Twin Tower in Yeouido, Seoul, on the 20th and unveiled this mid-to-long-term strategy. In his opening remarks, CEO Kim Dong-myung stated, "Now is a time of 'Value Shift,' where the growth value of the industry is being reorganized," adding, "Based on prepared capabilities and execution power, we will create tangible results without wavering."

The company's core strategy can be summarized in three main points: first, advancing the business portfolio; second, strengthening product and future competitiveness; and third, expanding the foundation for generating free cash flow. The most notable among these is the large-scale reorganization of the business structure.
ESS Emerges as New Growth Engine…Order Target Exceeds 90 GWh

CEO Kim Dong-myung diagnosed that the global ESS market is facing a faster-than-expected growth opportunity due to changes in power demand structure. He explained, "This growth momentum will not be evenly distributed to all battery companies but will be concentrated on a few companies that can meet local production and supply chain requirements," revealing LG Energy Solution's determination to be a leading player.

Accordingly, the company views the global ESS market as entering a phase of structural growth this year and has set its new order target to exceed last year's record high of 90 GWh. It also plans to nearly double its global ESS battery production capacity to over 60 GWh by the end of this year, with a significant portion of the expanded capacity focused on North America, the region with the steepest growth.

sum: It has been known since the start of series production in February that the car manufacturer is no longer outsourcing battery assembly for its second model based on the PPE platform to suppliers, but has taken it in-house. Together with Porsche Werkzeugbau GmbH, Porsche has established the Porsche Smart Battery Shop in Horná Streda. Located about an hour’s drive from Bratislava, the facility produces the battery modules that form the core of the Cayenne Electric’s battery – as we explained in detail in our technical deep dive. From Horná Streda, the modules are shipped to the supplier Webasto, who integrates the modules and power electronics into the battery frame before delivering them to the vehicle plant.

Porsche has now shared further details about the operations in Horná Streda in a dedicated announcement. The choice of location, which may initially seem unusual, was deliberate: the site was previously home to the Porsche Toolmaking division’s ‘Technology Centre’. “The facility has been expanded into an innovative technical centre that, as a dependable partner, supports Porsche in product and process development,” the car manufacturer stated.

On-site, the prototype construction capabilities of the Technology Centre were gradually expanded to include series production, with competencies being transferred accordingly. Construction of the hall for series production began in January 2023, and the first production systems were installed in September. The first modules for pre-series vehicles were produced there in May 2024.

In the production process, 32 prismatic cells supplied by LG Energy Solution are assembled into a complete module. Six of these modules are then combined in a battery frame with all the electronics to form a ready-to-install 113 kWh battery—the traditional battery pack is omitted in the electric Cayenne. Porsche describes the “complex, precisely orchestrated manufacturing process” in Horná Streda as follows:

After an initial inspection, the cells are prepared for further processing. The process begins with stack formation, where the cells are precisely stacked to ensure uniform alignment of the electrodes. These cell stacks are then inserted into their respective cell holders, and the cell tabs are positioned for the subsequent welding process.

sum: The South Korean battery maker LG Energy Solution will be taking a smaller share of the production from Electra Battery Materials’ Temiskaming-area cobalt refinery when commercial production kicks off next year.

Instead of scooping 80 per cent of the cobalt sulfate output from the plant, as originally agreed upon three years ago, Toronto-based Electra announced this week that LG will be taking 60 per cent under a revised offtake agreement.

By keeping 40 per cent of its production uncommitted, Electra explained in a March 10 news release that this latest contract is “providing flexibility for Electra to capture potential upside in pricing cycles.”
The company points to a more than 90 per cent increase in the price of cobalt sulfate since the start of 2025, “providing a constructive backdrop for Electra’s refining business.”
The refinery is located between the City of Temiskaming Shores and the Town of Cobalt. It’s scheduled to go into commercial production in late 2027.
The supply contract, or offtake agreement, with LG seemed due for an update. A pair of previous deals struck in 2022 and 2023 were predicated on the refinery entering production in 2025.

But delays in refinery construction and a longer-than-anticipated search for financing impacted the project timelines. Electra is now fully budgeted with $100 million to resume construction. Activity at the site is expected to ramp up by mid-year.

items.t: Tesla expands US LFP battery supply with LG Energy Solution deal: report

LG Energy Solution’s Lansing plant, formerly known as Ultium Cells 3, was previously operated as a joint venture with General Motors. LGES acquired GM’s stake in May 2025 and now fully owns the site. Is Vulcan Energy the Next Big Lithium Stock in Australia?
sum: Lithium stocks are back in the spotlight after a brutal two years, and one of the more interesting stories in the Australian lithium space is Vulcan Energy (VUL.ASX). It’s not riding the same price cycle as the rest. It’s playing a different game altogether, one built around geothermal energy, low cost, net-zero lithium from brines and Europe’s push for clean supply chains.

While most lithium companies spent 2025 cutting costs and shelving projects, Vulcan went the other way, signed up some of the biggest names in the European auto industry as customers and kept building. Let’s find out why, and if Vulcan Energy is a good investment.
- Vulcan is fully funded after securing a AUD$3.9 billion financing package and has started construction on its flagship Lionheart project in Germany.
- Major customers are already locked in, including Stellantis, Umicore, LG Energy Solution and Glencore, covering more than 70% of expected output.

- According to Bloomberg’s Analyst Recommendations, Vulcan Energy has 5 buy ratings, 0 holds, and 0 sells. The average analyst price target is AUD$7.40, signalling approximately 100% upside from current levels.

Vulcan Energy is developing a lithium project in Germany’s Upper Rhine Valley. But it’s not a mine in the traditional sense. Most lithium comes from one of two sources. Hard rock mining, think big open-pit mines in Western Australia, or extracting it from salty underground water known as brine, is commonly used in South America and China. Both traditional methods are energy-intensive and leave a significant environmental footprint.

More recently, the industry has been shifting towards a faster, cheaper method called adsorption-type direct lithium extraction (A-DLE), which pulls lithium from brine in hours rather than months using a special adsorbent material. It currently makes up around 10% of global lithium production, but it’s increasingly the method of choice, with major players like Rio Tinto backing it heavily, because of its low cost of production.

items.t: Soaring BESS sales narrow losses at Samsung, LG Energy Solution
sum: South Korea’s leading battery manufacturers LG Energy Solution (LGES) and Samsung SDI both reported narrower operating losses in the fourth quarter of 2025, as robust demand for battery energy storage system (BESS) helped offset continued weakness in electric vehicle sales.

LG Energy Solution posted an operating loss of KRW 122 billion ($85.5 million) for the October–December period, in line with guidance and down sharply from a KRW 226 billion loss a year earlier. Quarterly revenue rose 7.7% quarter-on-quarter to KRW 6.1 trillion, supported by strong BESS sales, particularly in North America. The company said the loss would have widened to KRW 455 billion without tax credits received under the US Inflation Reduction Act.

For full-year 2025, LGES reported KRW 23.7 trillion in revenue, down 7.6% year on year, while operating profit more than doubled to KRW 1.3 trillion, aided by BESS growth, improved cost efficiency, and North American production incentives.

“Last year, we saw a solid growth in ESS sales as we proactively expanded our LFP production capacity in North America, but total revenue decreased due to the slowdown in major customers’ EV sales,” said Chang Sil Lee, CFO of LG Energy Solution.

The manufacturer also said it successfully optimized its asset management in 2025 by reallocating capacity between EV and ESS production to limit new investments and improve idle-line utilization, establishing production sites early for mid- to low-end solutions such as high-voltage mid-nickel and LFP batteries in Europe, and enhancing capital efficiency through the sale of non-core assets, including a building from its North American joint venture facility.

For its energy storage products, LGES began local production of LFP batteries in North America in 2025 and plans to expand form factors from pouch-type to prismatic batteries. The company also strengthened its production competitiveness through system integration (SI) capabilities, resulting in a 140 GWh ESS order backlog.
Looking ahead, LGES expects global ESS installations to grow more than 40% in 2026, with North America accounting for roughly half of total battery demand.

items.t: LG Energy Solution pursuing battery deal for Tesla Optimus, other humanoid robots: report

Optimus is expected to be one of Tesla’s most ambitious projects, with Elon Musk estimating that the humanoid robot could be the company’s most important product.

LG Energy Solution shares jumped more than 11% on the 28th after a report from the Korea Economic Daily claimed that the company is pursuing battery supply and joint development agreements with several humanoid robot makers. These reportedly include Tesla, which is developing Optimus, as well as multiple Chinese robotics companies.

China is already home to several leading battery manufacturers, such as CATL and BYD, making the robot makers’ reported interest in LG Energy Solution quite interesting. Market participants interpreted the reported outreach as a signal that performance requirements for humanoid robots may favor battery chemistries developed by companies like LG.

According to the report, energy density is believed to be the primary reason humanoid robot developers are evaluating LG Energy Solution’s batteries. Unlike electric vehicles, humanoid robots have significantly less space available for battery packs while requiring substantial power to operate dozens of joint motors and onboard artificial intelligence processors.

LG Energy Solution’s ternary lithium batteries offer higher energy density compared with rivals’ lithium iron phosphate (LFP) batteries, which are widely used by Chinese EV manufacturers. That advantage could prove critical for humanoid robots, where runtime, weight, and compact packaging are key design constraints.

LG Energy Solution's Global Ambitions Hit by Credit Rating Downgrades
sum: [Korea Financial Times, Kim JaeHun] Various factors affect corporate value. Objective evaluation requires considering diverse variables. Korea Financial News aims to view a company's current situation, response, and financial soundness three-dimensionally through the 'Altman Z-Score' and examine the meanings hidden within in depth. [Editor's Note]

Since entering the stock market in early 2022, LG Energy Solution has executed aggressive annual facility investment (CAPEX) worth trillions of won for growth. In this process, borrowings increased, highlighting financial burden risks. Financial risks further emerged as profitability declined due to temporary slowdown in electric vehicle demand (chasm) immediately after listing.

This is why global credit rating agencies successively downgraded LG Energy Solution's credit rating this year. With domestic credit rating agencies' year-end regular evaluations remaining, the industry is closely watching the results.

Korea Financial Times calculated and analyzed LG Energy Solution's 'Altman Z-Score' from after listing to recently. The Altman Z-Score is an indicator that checks corporate financial risks based on financial statement items, with scores above 3 generally considered relatively stable for manufacturing businesses, and scores below 1.8 viewed as high risk.
LG Energy Solution's Z-score fell from 4.5 in 2022 immediately after listing to 3.99 in 2023 and 2.22 last year. While not reaching risk levels, it has been continuously declining since listing.

Looking at performance, in 2022 (consolidated basis) revenue was KRW 25.5986 trillion and operating profit was KRW 1.2137 trillion. Subsequently in 2023, revenue was KRW 33.7455 trillion and operating profit was KRW 2.1632 trillion, the highest ever, due to policy effects including the IRA (Inflation Reduction Act).
However, despite these results, the Z-score declined, analyzed as due to insufficient conversion to profit and cash generation compared to large-scale CAPEX and borrowing increases.

sum: Battery manufacturing engineers return to Hyundai-LG site in bitter epilogue

Two months after the largest immigration enforcement operation in American history convulsed a sprawling battery plant in rural Georgia, some of the detained South Korean engineers are trickling back to the worksite that became the centre of an international incident. By mid-November, approximately 50 engineers had re-entered the United States, their business visas restored without reapplication. More than 100 of the 317 South Korean nationals detained in the 4 September raid have now had their B-1 visas reinstated, according to representatives for the workers.

The phased return signals a cautious restoration of construction activity at the HL-GA Battery facility in Ellabell, a joint venture between Hyundai Motor Group and LG Energy Solution valued at $7.6bn ($8.1bn). Yet the resumption is anything but triumphant. It follows weeks of detention, diplomatic wrangling, and a rupture in trust that continues to shape investment decisions across South Korea's industrial sector.

Construction had been indefinitely suspended following the raid, which saw 475 individuals detained at the site. Federal authorities described it as necessary enforcement of immigration law. Many of the workers, however, were brought to Georgia specifically to install highly technical production equipment and train American personnel in battery cell manufacturing processes that remain scarce domestically. The tension between those objectives and the enforcement action has exposed deeper contradictions in America's approach to industrial policy.

According to LG Energy Solution, construction and business travel have resumed, with employees travelling to HL-GA and other US production facilities "with plans to expand the business travel gradually." The battery plant, when complete, will supply cells for electric vehicles (EVs) produced at Hyundai's adjacent Metaplant America assembly complex, which remains operational and unaffected by the enforcement action.

items.t: LG Energy Solution to expand LFP output in Korea
sum: LG Energy Solution Ltd. will begin mass production of lithium iron phosphate (LFP) batteries for energy storage systems (ESS) in South Korea in a move to expand its supply chain and strengthen the domestic battery industry.

The company announced the plan Monday at its Ochang plant in Cheongju, North Chungcheong Province, where it will start installing production lines by the end of the year. Output is scheduled to reach 1 GWh annually from 2027, with capacity increases to follow in line with market demand.

LG Energy Solution expects the project to lay the foundation for a domestic LFP industry. The company also anticipates steady growth in energy storage demand as renewable energy expands and sees the project as essential for improving energy security. It plans to focus on advancing technology and reinforcing its mass production capabilities.
The company said it will leverage research, testing and quality control expertise accumulated at the Ochang plant to sharpen its competitiveness in global markets.

Battery makers are seeking new growth drivers as demand for electric vehicle (EV) batteries temporarily slows. Because stability and cost efficiency are especially important in the energy storage sector, LFP batteries are becoming the preferred option.

More than 90 percent of the global ESS market currently uses LFP batteries. LG Energy Solution is the only major producer outside China manufacturing ESS-grade LFP batteries at scale. It already produces them at its Nanjing facility in China and began output at its Michigan plant in the United States in June. The company has secured an order backlog of about 120 GWh.

LFP batteries provide strong thermal stability and low ignition risk. Their thermal runaway onset temperature is about 270 degrees Celsius, significantly higher than that of nickel cobalt manganese or nickel cobalt aluminum batteries. Even if thermal runaway occurs, LFP batteries release almost no oxygen, which prevents flames and limits heat spread.

items.t: LG Energy Solution bets on homegrown LFP with 2027 launch
sum: LG Energy Solution has become the first Korean battery-maker to lock in a domestic production schedule for lithium iron phosphate batteries, reinforcing its position as the only non-Chinese producer of LFP cells amid accelerating worldwide demand for lower-cost, high-stability batteries.

The company said Monday that its Ochang plant in Cheongju, North Chungcheong Province, will begin commercial production of LFP batteries for energy storage systems in 2027, starting with one gigawatt hour of annual capacity. Installation of production lines will begin later this year, and LG Energy Solution plans to scale up output in line with rising market needs.

The decision marks a strategic shift for Korea’s top battery-maker, which already manufactures LFP products in the US and China but has yet to produce them at home. Executives say domestic output is crucial to strengthening Korea’s battery supply chain and positioning the firm for new growth in the rapidly expanding ESS sector.

“Ochang Energy Plant is LG Energy Solution’s ‘mother factory’ that serves as the hub for the development and manufacture of our entire product portfolio,” said Kim Hyung-sik, vice president and head of the company’s ESS battery division. “Producing LFP batteries for ESS here will mark the starting point for a new phase of challenge and growth in Korea’s ESS industry ecosystem.”

The domestic launch also enhances LG Energy Solution’s competitiveness in government-driven ESS projects, where policy incentives increasingly reward local production. The timing aligns with the Korea Power Exchange’s ongoing selection of contractors for the second round of bids for a 540 megawatt-hour ESS construction project slated for completion by the end of 2027 — the same year LG’s LFP lines come online.

Heightened competition was evident in the previous bidding round in July. Despite LG Energy Solution’s global ESS track record and a 120 gigawatt-hour order backlog, the company secured only 24 percent of total capacity with its LFP batteries. Samsung SDI swept the remaining 76 percent with its nickel-cobalt-aluminum cells, partly due to a lower bid price and the company’s domestic NCA production at its Ulsan plant. SK On won no share.
